A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S2T and S2T-LOCAL research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, selector-alignment measurements, latency results, and ablations in Tables 1–3 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds non-math evaluations, non-Qwen experiments, hyperparameter sweeps, uncertainty estimates, and selector-error analysis.

M1.justification: The core inference algorithm, reserved-token selector, and training losses remain unchanged. Appendix D.1 newly proposes an auxiliary ranking head parallel to the language-model head for models without reusable reserved tokens. This is an optional architectural adaptation; its evaluation is not reported.

E1.justification: Appendix F.2 and Table A5 add actual evaluations on TruthfulQA, ARC-Challenge, and MT-Bench, extending coverage to factuality, science question answering, and open-ended instruction following. The MATH-only training domain and original six evaluation benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains its comparator set, including DistilQwen2.5, TSD-KD, Maj@8, Mul-T, TaH, R2R, SpecReason, and Takeover. New appendix comparisons add dynamic candidate-sizing alternatives against fixed K and fine-tuned greedy decoding as a control for selector gains. The expanded baseline descriptions do not establish changes to the existing methods.

E3.justification: New experimental settings include Llama and Phi student–teacher pairings, MT-Bench judge scoring, parameter sweeps, and a 900-case agreement-based analysis. For existing experiments, the reported Qwen0.5B reserved-bin count changes from 16 to 12, and selector LoRA dropout changes from 0.1 to 0.05. These are reported setting revisions; unchanged Table 1 scores do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds reserved-bin and regularization sweeps, dynamic-versus-fixed candidate sizing, trigger-coverage sensitivity analyses, and a selector-disagreement study relating errors to final correctness. These investigate training stability, candidate coverage, and failure mechanisms beyond v1's retained ablations and trajectory examples.

E5.justification: Both versions already state averaging over three random seeds. v2 newly reports mean ± standard deviation for Greedy and S2T-LOCAL across both Qwen scales and all six main benchmarks in Table A6. Appendix F.6 also adds a correlation significance result for selector disagreements. No increase in run count is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, while v2 adds substantial domain, model, sensitivity, and error-analysis results. For example, new Table A8 reports Llama MATH500 accuracy of 27.8 for Greedy and 34.6 for S2T-LOCAL. Existing numerical corrections include the stated 0.5B math gain from 38% to 44.6%, MATH500 teacher entropy from 0.7 to 0.07, and appendix latency reduction from 75.8% to 74.8%.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies the scoring-bin anchors mathematically as v_i = (i − 1)/(|R| − 1), where v1 only described predefined bin values. This is a limited formal specification addition. The error decomposition, proposition, and numbered equations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central local-sufficiency and teacher-free selection contributions remain intact. The abstract and conclusion narrow the previously broad 24.1% improvement statement to a relative gain on the 1.5B model's Math Avg. score, making the headline claim more precisely scoped.

C2.justification: v2 replaces broad trigger-invariance language with a distinction between robust candidate coverage and trigger-dependent downstream accuracy. It adds interpretations of regularization tradeoffs, dynamic candidate-sizing failures, and benign versus harmful selector disagreements. It also qualifies DistilQwen2.5 as an off-the-shelf reference rather than a controlled training comparison.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access URL, baseline reproduction notes, fixed scoring anchors, an explicit regularization default, reserved-token compatibility guidance, and percentile calibration details for inference budgets. It clarifies that selector-training temperature differs from decoding temperature. However, v1's two-epoch selector-training statement and exact trigger-dataset counts are removed.

R1.justification: Appendix B.1 expands the distinction between S2T and speculative decoding, and references are added for TruthfulQA, ARC, Llama, and Phi. The overall research positioning remains stable. TSD-KD's author attribution and numerous publication updates refer to existing works rather than new comparison methods.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and selected results passages, reorganizes training details, swaps the evaluation and related-work appendices, and reorders supplementary analyses. It also updates affiliations and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The appendix gains nine tables covering sensitivity, new evaluations, uncertainty, and trigger diagnostics, substantially expanding the visual presentation. Existing tables are retained and renumbered, while figures are redistributed and several captions revised. The principal diagrams and plotted results remain visually stable.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the retained contribution: full S2T-LOCAL evaluation extends beyond Qwen, uncertainty is quantified for the main comparisons, and new sensitivity and error analyses expose when selection succeeds or fails. More precise claims and implementation disclosures address important weaknesses in v1. Reporting gaps remain, including unexplained Llama MMLU-Pro greedy scores of 19.5 in Table A7 versus 16.5 in Table A8 and some removed training details, but these do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and interpretability.
